result:
`bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is green (8 pass, 0 fail — the `ValidationException` trace in the output is pre-existing noise from the untouched `PostController` test).

**Summary:** `GET /health` now runs a real dependency check on every probe. I added `app/Health/HealthCheck.ts`, which resolves the Drizzle handle via `getDatabase()` from `config/database.ts` and runs a `select 1` round trip under a 2s timeout, returning a per-check `{ status, durationMs, message? }` result (`ok`/`error`, no caching), plus `runHealthChecks()` which assembles `{ status, checkedAt, checks: { db } }` and `healthStatusCode()` which maps a passing report to 200 and a failing one to 503. `app/Http/Controllers/HealthController.ts` renders that report with `this.json(report, { status })`, and `routes/web.ts` now points the unchanged, unauthenticated `/health` path at the controller instead of the static literal (the host-authorization exemption in `src/app.ts` is untouched). One supporting change was necessary: `app/Providers/DatabaseProvider.ts` previously let a boot-time connection failure propagate, which killed the process before it could ever answer a probe — it now logs and continues so an unreachable database surfaces as a 503 from `/health` rather than an app that will not start (the connection is retried on every `getDatabase()` call, so recovery is automatic). Tests live in `tests/HealthController.test.ts`: an HTTP test asserting 200 with `checks.db.status === 'ok'`, and unit tests covering the connect-failure, query-throws, and never-settles (timeout) paths plus the 503/200 status mapping. I also verified end-to-end out of band, with the database path made unopenable, that the endpoint answers `503 {"status":"error","checks":{"db":{"status":"error",…}}}`.
